claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The processed WTaTiVZr alloy is homogeneous while retaining nanoscale compositional disorder.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations in the WTaTiVZr alloy act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Dislocation pinning by nanoscale compositional fluctuations promotes more distributed plastic deformation.
More distributed plastic deformation delays localized failure in the WTaTiVZr alloy.
Complex grain-boundary structures in the WTaTiVZr alloy are effective obstacles to dislocation motion.
Compositional fluctuations create local variations in lattice parameters.
Compositional fluctuations create local variations in bonding.
Local variations in lattice parameters and bonding increase dislocation pinning.
Pure tungsten lacks the intrinsic dislocation obstacles attributed to the compositionally disordered WTaTiVZr alloy.
The relative lack of such obstacles in pure tungsten causes earlier strain localization and lower toughness.
At 800–1200°C, the WTaTiVZr alloy will exhibit higher yield strength than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
At 800–1200°C, the WTaTiVZr alloy will exhibit greater strain to failure than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
At 800–1200°C, the WTaTiVZr alloy will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
Microscopy will reveal dislocation pinning at nanoscale compositional interfaces in the WTaTiVZr alloy.
The proposed explanation applies when diffusion permits dynamic recovery and dislocation pinning is a critical deformation mechanism.
Different mechanisms may dominate at lower temperatures or different loading rates.
